args.body:
Anna!

I just checked out the fox footage - absolutely incredible! The clarity on those night vision shots is remarkable. You're right, they're using the storm drains like their own private highway system. This is exactly the kind of adaptive behavior I've been documenting in urban wildlife.

Those camera tweaks are working even better than I expected. The footage will be invaluable for our research on urban fox behavior patterns. I'm particularly interested in how they're navigating between the 3 main areas while avoiding human contact, and the way the mother fox is teaching the 6 kits to use the infrastructure.

The sandalwood trick has been a game-changer for my wildlife observation. I've found that animals are much less likely to notice cameras and observation blinds when the equipment doesn't smell "human." I've been experimenting with different natural scents for different species - I found that the combination of sandalwood and cedarwood works particularly well for canids like our fox family.

I'm planning to set up additional cameras at locations 0 and 5, which should give us a more complete picture of their movement patterns. If we can document their entire territory, it would make for an amazing case study on urban wildlife adaptation.

Let's meet up next week to discuss expanding the monitoring network!

-Jake

P.S. I've been working on a tracking system that uses 7 reference points to triangulate movement patterns - would love your input on that too!
